cls: Antihistamine (H1) with calcium-channel-blocking and antivertigo activity
pharm: Blocks histamine H1 receptors and inhibits calcium influx into vestibular and vascular smooth muscle cells, suppressing vestibular stimulation and producing antivertigo and antiemetic effects.
quick: Vertigo: 30 mg three times daily; motion sickness: 30 mg before travel

summary: Cinnarizine is a piperazine antihistamine with calcium-channel-blocking activity used for vestibular disorders (vertigo, tinnitus, nystagmus, nausea/vomiting of Meniere's disease and labyrinthine disorders) and for prevention of motion sickness. It suppresses vestibular over-activity and is sedating. Long-term use, particularly in the elderly, can cause extrapyramidal symptoms and drug-induced parkinsonism. It is not approved by the US FDA; it is licensed in many European, Asian, and other markets.
indications: Maintenance therapy of vestibular symptoms (vertigo, tinnitus, nystagmus, nausea and vomiting) of Meniere's disease and other labyrinthine disorders
Prevention and control of motion sickness
Symptomatic treatment of peripheral vascular disorders (in some markets)

moa: Cinnarizine antagonizes histamine H1 receptors and inhibits the influx of calcium ions through voltage-operated and receptor-operated calcium channels in vestibular sensory cells and vascular smooth muscle. By reducing the responsiveness of the labyrinth and suppressing nystagmus and other vestibular reflexes, it relieves vertigo, nausea, and motion sickness. Its calcium-channel-blocking action also produces mild vasodilation.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to cinnarizine or any excipient
relative: Elderly (risk of extrapyramidal symptoms and depression)
Conditions worsened by anticholinergic effects (e.g., glaucoma, prostatic hypertrophy)
monitor: Extrapyramidal symptoms / parkinsonism on long-term use
Weight gain and mood with chronic use

preg: Safety in pregnancy has not been established; avoid use unless the expected benefit outweighs any possible risk. Limited human data are available.
lact: It is not known whether cinnarizine is excreted in human milk; avoid use during breastfeeding because of limited data and the potential for sedation in the infant.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is described; use with caution in renal impairment and monitor for accumulation of CNS effects.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment, as cinnarizine is hepatically metabolized; no specific dose adjustment is established.

moderate: CNS depressants (alcohol, sedatives, hypnotics, opioids) - additive sedation
Tricyclic antidepressants and other anticholinergics - additive anticholinergic effects
minor: May reduce reaction time relevant to skin allergy testing (antihistamine effect)
interactions.food: Take after food to reduce gastric irritation.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol; it increases drowsiness and CNS depression.
interactions.diagnostics: Antihistamine effects can suppress skin allergy test responses; discontinue several days before testing.

serious: Extrapyramidal symptoms / drug-induced parkinsonism (especially elderly, long-term use)

monitoring: Daytime sedation and ability to drive/operate machinery
Extrapyramidal symptoms and tremor on chronic use, particularly in the elderly

missed: Take the missed dose when you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip it. Do not take a double dose.
overdose: Overdose may cause drowsiness, vomiting, tremor, hypotension, and, in children, central nervous system stimulation, seizures, or coma. There is no specific antidote; treat supportively with gastric lavage or activated charcoal if recent and appropriate, and monitor cardiovascular and neurologic status.
